submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole is the lower (GELU-trough) lobe of a layer-1 neuron and its strength is a positional-plus-token readout with no semantic or lookahead content: the first token of a prompt is always silent (pre-activation about +0.45 whatever it is), the second position sits at or near the trough for nearly any token (mean strength 0.13, all of 40 varied words negative), and from the third position on a token that is an ordinary word, punctuation, whitespace or subword fragment saturates it at 0.16-0.17, whereas a token that repeats one already seen (' for' repeated runs 0.17, 0.06, 0.00, then positive) or that follows a run of positively-reading content words ('Women patients children adults characters the' peaks at 0.010) stays positive and silent. The pole is therefore predicted active (peak at least 0.10) on almost any prompt of two or more ordinary tokens, and predicted inactive only where every token is silent - a lone first token, a repeated silent word ('women women' = 0.036), or a pure content-word run.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: theorem
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed top activating token appears as a lone first token, which the hypothesis says is always silent (pre-activation ~+0.45), so the trigger token in isolation must not fire this pole.
A single delimiter token as position one tests the first-token-silence rule against the massive-activation/delimiter confound: the hypothesis says no delimiter at position one can fire it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: children children
adversarial_test_results.detail: A content word repeated as the whole prompt, the analogue of the hypothesis's own 'women women' = 0.036, which the hypothesis says stays below the 0.10 active threshold.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: river river lake lake ocean ocean
adversarial_test_results.detail: An extended run of repeated content words with no function word to reset the trough tests whether the repetition-silence rule generalises past two tokens, as the hypothesis claims (peak stays at the position-two repeat value).

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Oxygen nitrogen carbon hydrogen helium lithium
adversarial_test_results.detail: A pure content-noun list in a science register with no function words or punctuation is exactly the 'pure content-word run' the hypothesis says peaks around 0.01 and never reaches 0.10.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Onions pan fry golden brown
adversarial_test_results.detail: Top example 2 with its function words stripped out leaves the same surface vocabulary but only content words, so the hypothesis predicts the run reads positive throughout and stays silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: believe already October year went fast
adversarial_test_results.detail: Top example 5's own content words in the same order but with the function words removed, testing whether it is the content words themselves that suppress the trough as the hypothesis claims rather than the specific trigger tokens.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Paris London Berlin Madrid Rome Vienna Tokyo
adversarial_test_results.detail: A run of capitalised proper nouns with no function word, punctuation or subword fragment is still a pure content-word run by the hypothesis's account, so it must not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Sunrise sunset noon midnight dawn dusk twilight then
adversarial_test_results.detail: A content-word run followed by a function word other than the one in the hypothesis's example ('then' rather than 'the') tests whether the claimed post-run suppression holds for any following function word.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Women patients children adults characters the theorem of was had upon ; , .
adversarial_test_results.detail: Every claimed trigger token appended to the hypothesis's own silent content run tests whether the retrospective suppression really persists, as the hypothesis says, leaving the whole prompt below 0.10 despite containing all of ' theorem', ' of', ' was', ' had', ' upon', ';', ',' and '.'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: qwx zpt lbv mrn kjd
adversarial_test_results.detail: Five meaningless ASCII fragments: the hypothesis says token identity is irrelevant and any ordinary subword fragment from position three on saturates the trough, so it must fire despite carrying no semantic content.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: 東京は日本の首都です。
adversarial_test_results.detail: A non-Latin-script sentence drawn from a different corpus genre; the hypothesis says byte-level subword fragments saturate the pole just like ordinary English words, so it must fire if the readout is truly token-agnostic.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE active = 1;
adversarial_test_results.detail: A SQL statement, a genre absent from the examples, contains ordinary words, punctuation and a delimiter, so the hypothesis predicts saturation from position three onward.
A prompt of digits and punctuation with no natural-language words at all must still fire if the pole is a positional-plus-token readout rather than a semantic one.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lemma follows directly from the triangle inequality.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Counterfactual minimal pair of top example 1 with only the claimed peak token changed (' theorem' to ' lemma'); a positional readout must still fire on the second position and then saturate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: When the tide went out at Wickstone, the whole shape of the harbour changed. Rocks that had been invisible for six hours surfaced in rows, dark and slick, and the gulls moved out to meet them. Marda had watched this happen every morning for forty years, first from her father's boat and then from the wall by the customs house, and she had never once seen it happen the same way twice. The council had promised in the spring to dredge the channel before the summer season, but the money had gone instead to repainting the cottages on the far side of the inlet, which now stood in colours that seemed to argue with one another: ochre beside violet, mint beside brick red, a pale yellow that turned almost white in the early light. Nobody could agree on what the town had looked like before the war, and after three long meetings the committee had simply voted, and the vote had been close. Marda had sat at the back of the room and said nothing at all. She had voted with the majority because the majority had promised to fix the drainage on Quay Street, which had flooded twice in January and once more in March, though the drainage was still not fixed and the water still came up through the grates whenever the wind turned south. The fishermen did not complain. They had learned, over many years, that complaining was a thing you did in the pub and not in the council chamber, and that the sea did what the sea did regardless of what any committee decided. On the morning I am describing, a man she did not recognise was standing at the end of the quay with a camera and a small notebook, writing down the names of the boats. She asked him what he was doing. He said he was making an inventory for the museum, because the museum had decided that the harbour was historically important and that everything in it ought to be recorded before it was changed. She told him that the harbour had already been changed a great deal and that nobody had recorded any of that, and he wrote that down too, which she found funny and also slightly insulting. They stood together for a while after that, watching the water come back over the rocks, and neither of them said anything more about it. Later, when the shops opened, she bought bread and a newspaper and walked home along the shore road, where the gorse was already beginning to go over and the blackthorn was in flower.
